title: Integration tests for a transactional notification enqueue
name: Notification enqueue tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these integration tests set up, isolate, or assert against the database? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In the concurrent dedupe test, what makes `a.id` equal `b.id` even though both calls run at the same time?
choices: Promise.all runs the two calls sequentially, so the second always sees the committed first row
The unique constraint on dedupe_key makes the second INSERT wait for the first transaction, then ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns no row and the service reads the committed id
The service holds a JavaScript-level lock per dedupe key
Each call gets its own TRUNCATE, so only one row can exist

questions.prompt: Why does the opt-out test also assert that the outbox has no 'push' row, rather than only checking the thrown error?
choices: To check that nothing was persisted on the error path, since the error is thrown inside the transaction that would have written both tables
Because the outbox is written before the preference check
Because vitest requires at least two assertions per test

questions.prompt: What would most likely happen if `afterAll(() => pool.end())` were removed?
choices: Tests would start failing with unique constraint violations
The test process could stay alive or warn about open handles because idle pool connections keep the event loop busy
The TRUNCATE in beforeEach would deadlock
